source.title: Unlocking the Abyss: A Dynamical Model for Deep-Sea Adventure Safety and Rescue Strategies

claim: Environmental motion prediction supplies a spatial search prior, while multi-objective equipment allocation supports deployment and Bayesian search updates.

manuscript_evidence.supports: Currents, density and seafloor support ARIMA/Monte Carlo forecasting, ridge spatial fields and a constrained Newtonian motion model.
Genetic multi-objective equipment selection minimizes cost/readiness time and maximizes availability.
Poisson-based grid prior follows predicted position; deploy, search and update probabilities using the paper's Bayesian model.
Extensions to other sea areas and multiple independent submersibles; search-interval sensitivity.

model_relationships.meaning: Forecast current uncertainty, regress fields and impose seabed boundary
Update after searching; the paper excludes searched cells

references.borrowed: Source Figure1 on physical PDFp4 was visually inspected. Preserve locate/prepare/search functional separation and the physical-spatial context.
references.not_borrowed: Source pixels, layout coordinates, paper-specific numerical results, team/award labels and unsupported causal claims.

caption: Overview of the deep-sea rescue framework. Environmental fields drive a constrained motion model and a spatial search prior. Multi-objective equipment allocation supports deployment. Search evidence updates grid probabilities for the next interval, with the source model's searched-cell exclusion made explicit. Sensitivity and geographic/multiple-target extensions are shown separately. All trajectories and grids are schematic.
